### Traits Structure Overview (`Traits`) {.topic-traits}

The [Traits]{.traits} table contains the list of [functional traits]{.traits} currently contained in [VegVault]{.vegvault}. The table contains one [Trait]{.traits} per row, with each [Trait]{.traits} containing: a unique [Trait ID]{.traits} (`trait_id`), original [Trait name]{.traits} from primary source (`trait_name`), and [Trait Domain]{.traits} (`trait_domain_id`). [Functional traits]{.traits} of vegetation [taxa]{.taxa} follow the same structure of [Dataset]{.database} and [Samples]{.database} obtained directly from [Dataset]{.database} [Source-Types]{.database}.

```{r}
#| label: Traits variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `Traits`."
data_comments_traits <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "trait_id", "ID of a Trait (unique)",
    "trait_domain_id", "ID of a Trait Domain",
    "trait_name", "Name of the trait from the primary source. See 'VegVault Content' for the details about the specific columns used from primary sources."
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "Traits"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_traits,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: Traits scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/Traits.svg"
  )
)
```

### Traits Domain (`TraitsDomain`) {.topic-traits}

```{r}
#| label: trait-domain-names
#| include: false

# The names and units as stored in the database; the names keep the
#   spelling of VegVault 1.0.0, such as "Plant heigh"
data_trait_domains <-
  dplyr::tbl(con, "TraitsDomain") %>%
  dplyr::select("trait_domain_name", "trait_unit") %>%
  dplyr::collect()

text_trait_domains <-
  knitr::combine_words(
    words = dplyr::pull(data_trait_domains, trait_domain_name),
    before = "`"
  )
```

Traits are grouped into [Trait Domains]{.traits} to allow for easier aggregation of [Traits]{.traits} across data sources.
As there are differences in trait names across sources of data and individual [Datasets]{.database}, the [VegVault]{.vegvault} database contains [Trait Domain]{.traits} information to group traits together.
In total, `r base::nrow(data_trait_domains)` [Trait Domains]{.traits} are present: `r text_trait_domains`, following [Diaz et al. (2016)](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature16489).
The names are stored as in VegVault 1.0.0, including the spelling `Plant heigh` for plant height.
Yet, it is up to the user to decide how to further aggregate trait values if multiple trait [Samples]{.database} of one [Trait Domain]{.traits} are available for the same environmental or taxonomic entity.

```{r}
#| label: TraitsDomain variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `TraitsDomain`."
data_comments_traits_domain <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "trait_domain_id", "ID of a Trait Domain (unique)",
    "trait_domain_name", "Name of the Trait Domain from Diaz et al. (2016)",
    "trait_unit", "Canonical unit used by all values in the Trait Domain",
    "trait_domain_description", "Additional information about the Trait Domain"
  )
load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "TraitsDomain"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_traits_domain,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: TraitsDomain scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/TraitsDomain.svg"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: show trait domains
#| tbl-cap: "Overview of Trait Domains and their associated Traits"
dplyr::tbl(con, "TraitsDomain") %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "Traits"),
    by = "trait_domain_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "TraitsValue"),
    by = "trait_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "Datasets") %>%
      dplyr::filter(dataset_type_id == 3),
    by = "dataset_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    trait_domain_id, trait_domain_name,
    trait_name,
    data_source_type_id, dataset_id
  ) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "DatasetSourceTypeID"),
    by = "data_source_type_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    trait_domain_id, trait_domain_name,
    trait_name,
    dataset_source_type
  ) %>%
  dplyr::collect() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(trait_domain_id, dataset_source_type) %>%
  dplyr::select(-trait_domain_id) %>%
  rlang::set_names(
    nm = c(
      "Trait domain",
      "Trait",
      "Data Source"
    )
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: trait per domain plot

n_traits_per_domain <-
  dplyr::inner_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "TraitsDomain"),
    dplyr::tbl(con, "Traits"),
    by = "trait_domain_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(trait_domain_name, trait_name) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(trait_domain_name) %>%
  dplyr::count(name = "N") %>%
  dplyr::collect() %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# The figures show the domain names in plain spelling; the database keeps
#   the names of VegVault 1.0.0 ("Plant heigh", "Leaf Area")
vec_domain_labels <-
  c(
    "Plant heigh" = "Plant height",
    "Leaf Area" = "Leaf area"
  )

fig_n_traits_per_domain <-
  n_traits_per_domain %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    trait_domain_label = dplyr::coalesce(
      base::unname(vec_domain_labels[trait_domain_name]),
      trait_domain_name
    ),
    # Alphabetical from the top, as in the figure of the trait values
    trait_domain_label = factor(
      trait_domain_label,
      levels = base::sort(base::unique(trait_domain_label), decreasing = TRUE)
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    ggplot2::aes(
      y = N,
      x = trait_domain_label
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Traits per trait domain",
    x = "",
    y = "Number of traits"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = "none"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip(
    ylim = c(0, base::max(dplyr::pull(n_traits_per_domain, N)) + 1.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = trait_domain_label,
      xend = trait_domain_label,
      yend = 0
    ),
    color = col_black,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    fill = col_white,
    size = point_size,
    shape = 21,
    col = col_black,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_label(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      label = scales::label_comma()(N)
    ),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = point_size * 2,
    family = font_family,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  )

save_figure_to_render(fig_n_traits_per_domain)
```

### Traits value (`TraitsValue`) {.topic-traits}

In general, data of functional traits of vegetation taxa follow the same structure of the [Dataset]{.database} and [Samples]{.database} obtained directly from the [Dataset Source-Types]{.database}. Therefore, `TraitsValue` table contains not only the actual measured value of [Trait]{.traits} observation but also information about linking information across [Datasets]{.database}, [Samples]{.database}, and [Taxa]{.taxa}. This comprehensive linkage ensures that each Trait value is accurately associated with its relevant ecological, environmental and taxonomic context.

Since VegVault 2.0.0, every trait value is stored in the unit of its [Trait Domain]{.traits} (`trait_unit` of `TraitsDomain`), shown in the table below.
Each value references exactly one versioned conversion rule of `TraitUnitConversion` and, when it is derived from another trait, one derivation rule of `TraitDerivation`, such as the reciprocal that turns specific leaf area (SLA) into leaf mass per area (LMA).
The values and units as the data providers reported them are not stored in the database; they are part of the trait data release ([VegVault-Trait_data](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24505585)), together with the audit tables of the conversion.

```{r}
#| label: trait domain units
#| tbl-cap: "Unit of the values of each Trait Domain."
data_trait_domains %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    `Trait Domain` = trait_domain_name,
    `Unit` = trait_unit
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```


```{r}
#| label: TraitsValue variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `TraitsValue`."
data_comments_traits_value <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "trait_id", "ID of a Trait",
    "dataset_id", "ID of a Dataset",
    "sample_id", "ID of a Sample",
    "taxon_id", "ID of a Taxon",
    "trait_value", "Value of specific measured observation of Trait.",
    "trait_unit_conversion_id", "ID of the required unit conversion rule",
    "trait_derivation_id", "ID of an optional derived-trait rule"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "TraitsValue"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_traits_value,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: TraitsValue scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/TraitsValue.svg"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: trait value occurences plot

n_occurences_per_dommain <-

  ) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(

    by = "trait_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(trait_domain_name) %>%

  dplyr::collect() %>%

fig_n_occurences_per_dommain <-
  n_occurences_per_dommain %>%

    trait_domain_label = dplyr::coalesce(

    trait_domain_label = factor(
      trait_domain_label,
      levels = base::sort(base::unique(trait_domain_label), decreasing = TRUE)
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    ggplot2::aes(
      y = N,
      x = trait_domain_label
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    transform = scales::transform_log10(),
    breaks = c(1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e7, 1e8),
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip(
    ylim = c(1e4, 1e8)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Trait values per trait domain",
    x = "",
    y = "Number of trait values"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = "none"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = trait_domain_label,
      xend = trait_domain_label,
      yend = 0
    ),
    color = col_black,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    fill = col_white,
    size = point_size,
    shape = 21,
    col = col_black,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_label(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      label = scales::label_comma()(N)
    ),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = point_size * 2,
    family = font_family,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(0.5)
  )

save_figure_to_render(fig_n_occurences_per_dommain)
```

### Trait Unit Conversion (`TraitUnitConversion`) {.topic-traits}

The `TraitUnitConversion` table holds the rules that bring the value of each data provider to the unit of its [Trait Domain]{.traits}, one rule per row.
A rule applies to one trait of one provider, and sometimes only to one dataset of that provider, and it is kept under a unique name and a version, so that every stored value can be traced to the rule that converted it.

```{r}
#| label: TraitUnitConversion variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `TraitUnitConversion`."
data_comments_trait_unit_conversion <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "trait_unit_conversion_id", "ID of a conversion rule (unique)",
    "conversion_rule_key", "Name of the rule (unique), for example `try_leaf_area_3112_cm2`",
    "rule_version", "Version of the rule",
    "source_provider", "Data provider the rule applies to (`TRY` or `BIEN`)",
    "source_trait_id", "Trait of the data provider the rule applies to",
    "source_dataset_key", "Dataset of the data provider the rule is limited to (empty for all datasets)",
    "normalized_original_unit", "Unit as the data provider reported it, written in one standard way",
    "standardized_unit", "Unit after the conversion, the unit of the Trait Domain",
    "trait_dimension", "Physical dimension of the trait, for example `length` or `area`",
    "operation", "Kind of conversion: `identity`, `multiply` or `reciprocal`",
    "multiplier", "Factor of the conversion",
    "evidence", "Reason or source of the rule"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "TraitUnitConversion"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_trait_unit_conversion,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

### Trait Derivation (`TraitDerivation`) {.topic-traits}

The `TraitDerivation` table holds the rules that compute one trait from another after its unit conversion, such as leaf mass per area from specific leaf area.

```{r}
#| label: TraitDerivation variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `TraitDerivation`."
data_comments_trait_derivation <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "trait_derivation_id", "ID of a derivation rule (unique)",
    "derivation_rule_key", "Name of the rule (unique), for example `sla_to_lma`",
    "rule_version", "Version of the rule",
    "input_unit", "Unit of the trait the rule starts from",
    "output_unit", "Unit of the derived trait",
    "trait_dimension", "Physical dimension of the derived trait",
    "operation", "Kind of derivation, for example `reciprocal`",
    "multiplier", "Factor of the derivation",
    "evidence", "Reason or source of the rule"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "TraitDerivation"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_trait_derivation,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: TraitUnitConversion scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/TraitUnitConversion.svg"
  )
)
```

### Traits Reference (`TraitsReference`) {.topic-traits}

To ensure clarity and reproducibility, each [Trait]{.traits} in [VegVault]{.vegvault} can have additional [References]{.database} beyond the general [Dataset]{.database} and [Sample]{.database} [References]{.database}. These [Trait]{.traits}-specific [References]{.database} provide detailed provenance and citation information, supporting rigorous scientific research and enabling users to trace the origins and validation of each trait value. 

```{r}
#| label: TraitsReference variables scheme structure
#| tbl-cap: "Column names and types for table `TraitsReference`."
data_comments_traits_reference <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~column_name, ~description,
    "trait_id", "ID of a Trait",
    "reference_id", "ID of a Reference"
  )

load_db_table_data_types(
  con,
  "TraitsReference"
) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_comments_traits_reference,
    by = "column_name"
  ) %>%
  plot_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: TraitsReference scheme structure
build_absolute_graphics_include(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/website/DB_scheme_visualisation/TraitsReference.svg"
  )
)
```
